experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Visit the iconic Gyeongbokgung Palace, the largest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces, and rent a traditional Hanbok to wear while exploring the grounds. Wearing Hanbok grants free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial changing of the royal guard and explore the National Folk Museum located within the palace complex.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Seoul's vibrant food scene at one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of traditional Korean market culture.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Experience & SM Town COEX Artium
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Korea's global K-pop phenomenon at SM Town COEX Artium, a multi-story entertainment complex dedicated to SM Entertainment's top artists including EXO, aespa, and NCT. Explore interactive exhibits, hologram theaters, and exclusive merchandise. Afterward, head to the nearby Hanteo Chart Music Awards area and explore the K-Star Road in Apgujeong, lined with bear statues representing top K-pop groups.

experiences.name: Insadong & Bukchon Hanok Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming Insadong district, known for its traditional tea houses, art galleries, and unique Korean craft shops. Then walk to the stunning Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of over 900 traditional Korean hanok houses dating back to the Joseon Dynasty. Enjoy panoramic views of the city skyline contrasted against ancient rooftops, and stop for a traditional tea ceremony at a local teahouse.

experiences.name: Korean Cooking Class & Makgeolli Pairing
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Korean cooking class in the trendy Mapo-gu district where a local chef guides you through preparing classic dishes such as kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew), pajeon (Korean savory pancakes), and japchae (glass noodle stir-fry). The class concludes with a traditional makgeolli (Korean rice wine) pairing session, giving you deep insight into Korean culinary traditions and fermentation culture that you can recreate at home.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Seoul Station — budget-friendly at around ₩9,500. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Convenience store snacks near hotel — budget ₩3,000–₩6,000

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy for Day 2. Exchange some currency at the airport (Incheon has competitive rates) or use a Wise/Revolut card. Pick up a T-money card at the airport for public transit use throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a slow morning to recover from travel. Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace — one of Seoul's most iconic landmarks. Arrive early (opens 09:00) to beat crowds. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) near the palace entrance for around ₩15,000–₩20,000, which also grants free entry to the palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautiful traditional Korean village with preserved hanok houses, just a short walk from the palace. Stroll the narrow alleys and soak in the K-drama atmosphere. Then head to Insadong for cultural shopping — browse traditional crafts, tea houses, and street snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard for indie shops and street food. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday lights. Head back to the hotel via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours, budget ₩3,000–₩5,000
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market (short taxi/subway ride) — try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) or mayak gimbap, budget ₩4,000–₩8,000
meals.dinner: Insadong street food — hotteok, tteokbokki, and odeng (fish cake soup), budget ₩5,000–₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (around -5°C to 5°C). Dress in warm layers. Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays, so Wednesday is perfect. T-money card makes subway rides seamless.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is stunning even in winter. Book tickets in advance online — entry is around ₩8,000 for the Secret Garden tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Jongmyo Shrine, a serene royal ancestral shrine and another UNESCO site. Then head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a peaceful winter stroll along the illuminated waterway — free and beautifully decorated in December.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark lit up beautifully at night. Browse the nearby Dongdaemun night market for budget fashion and street food.

meals.breakfast: Juk (Korean rice porridge) at a local jukjip near the hotel — budget ₩5,000–₩7,000
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village alley restaurants — try Korean set meals (백반, baekban), budget ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun street food stalls — tteokbokki, sundae, and corn dogs, budget ₩5,000–₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Cheonggyecheon Stream often has a winter light festival in December — check local listings for special events. DDP area is great for night photography.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Myeongdong, Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. In the morning it's less crowded — explore cosmetic shops (Innisfree, Etude House, The Face Shop) for affordable K-beauty products. Window shop or pick up gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) via the Namsan Cable Car (₩10,000 round trip) or hike up for free. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul. See the famous love locks and take in the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the famous evening street food scene — the streets come alive with vendors. Try Korean corn dogs, grilled skewers, and pajeon. Explore the area's festive Christmas decorations.

meals.breakfast: Myeongdong Kyoja area — grab a simple kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup), budget ₩9,000
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — tteokbokki, hotteok, egg bread (계란빵), budget ₩6,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja restaurant — famous kalguksu and mandu (dumplings), budget ₩9,000–₩13,000

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely popular on weekends, so enjoy the slightly calmer Friday morning. Many cosmetic shops offer free samples — a great way to try K-beauty products without spending.

day_by_day.morning: Take a subway to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the heart of Seoul's youth culture, K-indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant murals and quirky cafes in the morning when it's calmer. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or just enjoy the street art for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sangsu-dong and Mangwon-dong neighborhoods nearby — charming, artsy, and very local. Browse vintage shops and indie boutiques. Visit Mangwon Market for a local market experience far from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the famous Saturday night busking performances — K-pop dance crews, indie musicians, and street performers entertain for free. Enjoy the electric atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Trendy Hongdae café — try Dalgona coffee or a Korean-style brunch, budget ₩5,000–₩8,000
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — fresh tteok (rice cakes), bindaetteok, and local snacks, budget ₩5,000–₩8,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae area — samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a local BBQ restaurant, budget ₩12,000–₩15,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturday nights in Hongdae are legendary. The area is safe but very busy — keep belongings secure. Many restaurants in Hongdae have English menus or picture menus.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park on the northern edge of Seoul — a stunning mountain park perfect for a winter hike. Take the subway to Gupabal Station and hike to Bukhansanseong Fortress. Entry is free. The mountain views in winter with snow are breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the hike and head to Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming, less touristy alternative to Bukchon. Explore indie cafes, art galleries, and traditional alley architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a Korean jjimjilbang (sauna/bathhouse) — budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 for entry. Dragon Hill Spa near Yongsan is a popular, affordable option. Unwind after the hike with heated rooms, saunas, and communal rest areas.

meals.breakfast: Pack convenience store kimbap and snacks for the hike, budget ₩3,000–₩5,000
meals.lunch: Post-hike doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) at a local restaurant near the park, budget ₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or nearby Korean restaurant — bibimbap or sundubu jjigae, budget ₩8,000–₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Bukhansan hike. Trails can be icy in December — microspikes or trail crampons are recommended and can be rented near the trailhead. The jjimjilbang is a quintessential Korean cultural experience — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Itaewon and the adjacent Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood — historically multicultural and now a trendy area with diverse food options and independent boutiques. Visit the War Memorial of Korea nearby — free entry and very informative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market — one of Asia's largest electronics bazaars. Even if not buying, it's a fascinating cultural experience. Then visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — free entry and world-class exhibits on Korean history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon's evening scene — browse international restaurants and K-pop merchandise stores. Visit a norebang (Korean karaoke room) for a classic K-culture experience — budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 per hour per room.

meals.breakfast: Haebangchon local café — coffee and pastry, budget ₩4,000–₩6,000
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria or nearby Korean restaurant — bibimbap or dosirak (lunch box), budget ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Itaewon — try Korean fried chicken (chimaek) with beer at a local chicken joint, budget ₩12,000–₩18,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is free and absolutely worth 2–3 hours. Norebang is a must-do Korean cultural activity — it's private rooms, so perfect for solo travelers or groups.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour south of Seoul by subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station, then bus or taxi). Walk the fortress walls for sweeping winter views. Entry is ₩1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and the traditional market nearby. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress complex. Enjoy the quiet, less touristy atmosphere compared to Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Head to Gangnam district for evening exploration — walk the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard, see the affluent neighborhood immortalized by Psy's hit song, and browse the underground COEX Mall.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store before departure, budget ₩3,000–₩5,000
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (short rib BBQ) — Suwon is famous for this dish, budget ₩15,000–₩20,000 (a worthy splurge)
meals.dinner: Gangnam underground food court at COEX Mall — diverse Korean options, budget ₩8,000–₩13,000

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is easily accessible by Seoul subway — no need for a separate ticket if using T-money. The fortress walk takes about 2–3 hours for the full circuit. Dress very warmly as it's exposed to wind.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Korean Folk Village in Yongin (about 1 hour from Seoul by subway + shuttle). Experience traditional Korean village life, folk performances, and seasonal winter activities. Entry is around ₩15,000–₩20,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Folk Village — watch traditional crafts demonstrations, see tightrope walking performances, and explore the recreated Joseon-era buildings. Great for immersive K-culture experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Visit Lotte World Mall or nearby Seokchon Lake — beautifully lit for the holiday season. Enjoy the Christmas Eve Eve atmosphere with locals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby bakery before departure, budget ₩4,000–₩6,000
meals.lunch: Korean Folk Village food stalls — traditional dishes like haemul pajeon and sikhye (sweet rice drink), budget ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Jamsil area near Lotte World — Korean BBQ or hot pot restaurant, budget ₩12,000–₩18,000

day_by_day.notes: Korean Folk Village often has special winter and Christmas season events in December. Check their website for the performance schedule. The shuttle bus from Suwon Station or direct buses from Seoul make this accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Free to enter. Beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round, and may have special winter decorations. A peaceful and culturally rich morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gwangjang Market in depth — one of Seoul's oldest traditional markets. Try the famous mayak gimbap, raw beef yukhoe, and bindaetteok. Browse fabrics and traditional goods.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong Cathedral — a stunning Gothic cathedral lit beautifully for Christmas. Koreans celebrate Christmas enthusiastically. Enjoy the festive street atmosphere, Christmas markets, and lights. Many young Koreans treat Christmas Eve like Valentine's Day — the city is magical.

meals.breakfast: Insadong tea house — traditional Korean tea and tteok (rice cake), budget ₩5,000–₩8,000
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — mayak gimbap and bindaetteok, budget ₩6,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Christmas street food feast — splurge a little on the holiday, budget ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most festive nights in Seoul. Myeongdong and Hongdae are packed with couples and young people celebrating. Public transit runs late on Christmas Eve — check schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas is a public holiday in South Korea! Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (smaller, less visited) for a quiet morning. Then walk to Deoksugung Palace and do the famous Deoksugung Stonewall Road (돌담길) — a romantic tree-lined path perfect for a peaceful Christmas morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Han River (Hangang Park) — rent a bicycle if weather permits or simply walk along the river. The Han River parks are beloved by locals. Visit Yeouido Hangang Park for beautiful winter riverside views.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate Christmas dinner Korean style — visit a Korean BBQ restaurant for a festive meat feast. Try Mapo Galmaegi-sal street for affordable pork restaurants. Toast the holiday with Korean soju or makgeolli.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store Christmas morning treats — sweet breads and warm drinks, budget ₩4,000–₩6,000
meals.lunch: Yeouido area restaurant — Korean army stew (budae jjigae), a hearty winter dish, budget ₩10,000–₩13,000
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ Christmas dinner — pork belly or beef bulgogi with all the banchan, budget ₩15,000–₩20,000

day_by_day.notes: Some attractions may have adjusted hours on Christmas Day. Many Korean restaurants remain open. The Han River is a beloved local gathering spot — even in winter, Koreans brave the cold for riverside walks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123rd floor) — one of the world's tallest buildings with stunning Seoul panoramas. Entry is around ₩27,000 — a worthy splurge for the view. Best visited on a clear winter morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the adjacent Stone Village (Seokchon Lake area) and nearby Jamsil neighborhood. Visit the Olympic Park from the 1988 Seoul Olympics — free entry, large green space with public art installations and the KSPO Dome.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hongdae for a final Saturday night out. Enjoy live music at a small indie venue or catch busking performances. Browse the late-night street stalls and enjoy the youthful energy one last time.

meals.breakfast: Jamsil area café — coffee and Korean-style toast (계란 토스트), budget ₩4,000–₩7,000
meals.lunch: Olympic Park area — packed lunch from a nearby convenience store or local kimbap restaurant, budget ₩5,000–₩8,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae final dinner — try budae jjigae (army stew) or japchae with a group, budget ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: The Lotte World Tower observation deck requires advance booking on weekends. The Olympic Park is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — worth the visit for history and art lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul. Revisit a favorite neighborhood or spot for last photos. Head back to Insadong or Myeongdong for any last-minute souvenir shopping — Korean snacks (Pepero, honey butter chips, seaweed), K-beauty products, and traditional crafts make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final Korean meal. Visit a local neighborhood market or simply relax at a cozy café. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX from Seoul Station (about 43 minutes, ₩9,500). Arrive at least 3 hours before international departure. Enjoy duty-free shopping at the airport and reflect on an amazing 13-day Seoul adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — haejang-guk (hangover soup/hearty beef soup), a classic Korean morning meal, budget ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.lunch: Airport or final restaurant near hotel — Korean set meal (백반), budget ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport food court or grab snacks for the flight, budget ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: Return or refill your T-money card balance at any subway station — unused balance can be refunded. Keep receipts for VAT refund on purchases over ₩30,000 at participating stores — claim at the airport before departure. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then take the AREX Express Train or airport limousine bus to your hotel in Seoul (approx. 50–70 min). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel — look for a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) for kimbap, ramen, or hotteok to tide you over after arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you've had a long flight. Hydrate, rest, and prepare for a full Day 2. Exchange some currency at the airport (Incheon has great rates) and pick up a T-money card for public transit.

day_by_day.morning: Start slow with a late breakfast at the hotel, then head to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — Seoul's most iconic royal palace. Arrive early to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 AM & 2:00 PM). Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop for free or discounted palace entry and beautiful photos in the palace grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) — a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses with stunning views of the city. Then explore nearby Insadong (인사동) for K-culture souvenirs, traditional tea houses, and street art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard complex, browse indie shops and local crafts, then head to Gwanghwamun Square for a night view of the illuminated palace and Admiral Yi Sun-sin statue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try a traditional Korean breakfast of doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) and rice at a local restaurant
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — famous ginseng chicken soup, a Seoul institution (approx. ₩17,000–₩20,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong area — try Sanchon (산촌) for a beautiful temple food-inspired Korean set meal, or a cozy Korean BBQ spot in the neighborhood (approx. ₩15,000–₩25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (avg. 0–5°C / 32–41°F). Dress in warm layers. The hanbok rental shops near Gyeongbokgung open around 9:00–10:00 AM. Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) — one of Seoul's most beautiful royal gardens, especially atmospheric in winter. Book the Secret Garden guided tour in advance (runs several times daily, approx. ₩8,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Jongno district and explore Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated in winter. Then walk to Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) for a peaceful riverside stroll through the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a stunning futuristic architecture landmark by Zaha Hadid. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun market area, famous for fashion, fabric, and late-night shopping culture.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest markets, try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls) for a quintessential local breakfast experience
meals.lunch: Grab lunch near Changdeokgung — try a local hansik (Korean cuisine) restaurant for bibimbap or doenjang jjigae set (approx. ₩10,000–₩15,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — try Mukbang Hof or a local pojangmacha (street food tent) for tteokbokki, sundae, and Korean fried chicken with beer (approx. ₩15,000–₩20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are limited in winter — book online at the Cultural Heritage Administration website. Gwangjang Market opens early (around 8:00 AM), perfect for breakfast.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's vibrant youth and K-culture hub. Explore the street art, murals, and quirky indie shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or Line Friends flagship store for a fun K-pop culture experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area — beautiful campus architecture and trendy shopping streets. Then head to the nearby Han River (Hangang) at Yeouido for a winter riverside walk and views of the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for its famous nightlife, live street performances (busking), and K-indie music scene. Explore the clubs, live music venues, and late-night cafés that make Hongdae iconic.

meals.breakfast: Hip café in Hongdae — try Café Bora (known for purple taro lattes and Korean-inspired drinks) or a local bakery café for coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Hongdae street food crawl — try hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, and Korean corn dogs from street vendors (approx. ₩5,000–₩10,000 total)
meals.dinner: Hongdae — Yoogane Dak Galbi (유가네 닭갈비) for spicy stir-fried chicken with rice, or a trendy Korean fusion restaurant in the area (approx. ₩15,000–₩22,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is most lively in the evening. Street busking performances typically start around 6–7 PM. The area is very walkable and well-connected by subway (Hongik University Station, Line 2).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) — one of the most unique and historically significant experiences in Korea. Book a guided DMZ tour from Seoul (departs ~8:00 AM, returns ~4:00–5:00 PM). Visit the Joint Security Area (JSA) at Panmunjom, the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory, and Dorasan Station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Included in the DMZ tour — continue exploring the various DMZ sites with your guide. The JSA tour requires advance booking through an authorized tour operator (approx. ₩100,000–₩130,000 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul in the late afternoon. Decompress with dinner in the Itaewon or Myeongdong area. Explore Myeongdong's famous night market for street food and shopping.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the tour departs — or grab a convenience store breakfast on the way
meals.lunch: Lunch included at a rest stop near the DMZ, or bring snacks — tour operators typically arrange a lunch stop
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Night Market — try Korean street food like grilled squid, cheese lobster tails, egg bread, and hotteok (approx. ₩10,000–₩15,000 for a full street food dinner)

day_by_day.notes: The DMZ/JSA tour must be booked at least 2–3 days in advance. Bring your passport — it is required for entry. Dress warmly as the DMZ area is very exposed and cold in December. Tours depart from major hotels or Dongdaemun area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower (남산서울타워) — take the cable car up for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Explore the famous love lock wall and enjoy the crisp mountain air. The tower observatory offers 360-degree city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the charming Namsangol Hanok Village at the base of Namsan — a beautifully restored traditional village with free entry, cultural performances, and artisan demonstrations. Then explore the hip Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood nearby — a multicultural enclave with indie cafés and international eateries.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Itaewon (이태원) for the evening — Seoul's most international neighborhood with diverse restaurants, rooftop bars, and a lively atmosphere. Explore Gyeongnidan-gil (경리단길) — a trendy street lined with unique restaurants and concept cafés.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Namsangol area or Haebangchon — try a cozy Korean restaurant for sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal (approx. ₩10,000–₩14,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon/Gyeongnidan-gil — choose from a wide variety of cuisines. For a Korean experience, try Maple Tree House for premium Korean BBQ, or explore the many mid-range options (approx. ₩20,000–₩35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower is open daily. The cable car runs from 10:00 AM. On clear winter days, visibility from the tower can extend for miles. Namsangol Hanok Village is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Gangnam (강남) district — Seoul's upscale southern neighborhood made famous by Psy's song. Visit COEX Mall (one of Asia's largest underground malls) and the stunning Starfield Library inside. Walk through the Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) — a beautiful Buddhist temple dramatically situated amidst Gangnam's skyscrapers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Garosu-gil (가로수길) — tree-lined streets with luxury boutiques, K-beauty flagship stores, and trendy cafés. This is the heart of Korean celebrity and fashion culture. Visit SM Entertainment's SM Town Museum for a deep dive into K-pop.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a K-pop culture evening — attend a fan café gathering, visit a K-pop merchandise store in Gangnam, or check if any idol group fan meetings or showcase events are happening. Alternatively, enjoy the glittering Gangnam nightscape from a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Garosu-gil or Apgujeong café — try a Korean-style brunch at a trendy concept café with eggs, toast, and Korean sides
meals.lunch: COEX Food Court or a restaurant in the Gangnam area — try galbi tang (beef short rib soup) or Korean BBQ lunch special (approx. ₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Gangnam — try Hanilkwan (한일관) for classic Korean cuisine including galbi and bulgogi in an elegant setting (approx. ₩25,000–₩40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: COEX Starfield Library is free to enter and makes for a spectacular photo stop. Check the SM Town website for any scheduled events. Garosu-gil is most lively on weekday afternoons and evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon (수원) — about 1 hour from Seoul by subway. Visit Hwaseong Fortress (화성), a magnificent UNESCO World Heritage Site — a massive fortress wall you can walk along for panoramic views of the city and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress walls. Then visit the Korean Folk Village (한국민속촌) nearby — a living open-air museum recreating traditional Korean village life with artisan demonstrations, folk performances, and historical architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to the lively Hongdae or Sinchon area for a relaxed evening. Visit a norebang (노래방) — a private karaoke room — for a quintessential Korean cultural experience with friends.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Suwon
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous throughout Korea for its galbi (beef short ribs). Try a local restaurant near Hwaseong for this regional specialty (approx. ₩20,000–₩30,000)
meals.dinner: Korean Folk Village area or back in Seoul — try a comforting bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant (approx. ₩10,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Take subway Line 1 from Seoul Station to Suwon Station (approx. 1 hour, ₩2,500). Korean Folk Village is a separate entry from Hwaseong Fortress — plan your time accordingly. Both sites are best visited on the same day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the vibrant Mangwon Market (망원시장) — a beloved local market less touristy than Gwangjang, popular with young Seoulites. Browse fresh produce, Korean street snacks, and local specialties. Then walk along the nearby Mangwon Hangang Park for a peaceful morning riverside stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the trendy Mapo district and explore Yeonnam-dong (연남동) — a hipster neighborhood with charming cafés, independent bookshops, and creative restaurants along a converted railway greenway (Gyeongui Line Forest Park). Perfect for slow afternoon wandering.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a traditional Korean jjimjilbang (찜질방) — a Korean bathhouse and sauna. Try Dragon Hill Spa (용산구) or Siloam Sauna near Seoul Station for a full Korean spa experience: hot baths, saunas, body scrubs, and relaxation rooms. A perfect mid-trip recharge.

meals.breakfast: Mangwon Market — try fresh kimbap, egg rolls, and hotteok from market stalls (approx. ₩3,000–₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Yeonnam-dong — choose from one of the many creative cafés and restaurants. Try a Korean brunch spot or a trendy ramen restaurant (approx. ₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or nearby — many jjimjilbangs have on-site restaurants serving sikhye (sweet rice drink), eggs, and Korean comfort food. Or try a nearby neighborhood restaurant (approx. ₩10,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jjimjilbang entry typically costs ₩10,000–₩15,000 and includes a locker, towel, and traditional Korean shorts/shirt. Most are open 24 hours. Dragon Hill Spa is one of the most famous and offers multiple themed sauna rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. Free entry, plan for 2–3 hours. Located in Yongsan, easily accessible by subway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's premier shopping and beauty district. Browse K-beauty flagship stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), sample street food, and soak in the festive Christmas Eve atmosphere. Myeongdong Cathedral is beautifully illuminated for Christmas.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Enjoy the festive lights and decorations throughout the city. Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for the winter light festival, or visit Lotte World Tower at Jamsil for spectacular Christmas illuminations and a possible fireworks display.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food — a full meal of Korean street snacks: tteokbokki, tornado potato, Korean fried chicken skewers, and hotteok (approx. ₩10,000–₩15,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner — try a mid-range Korean restaurant for a festive meal. Consider Tosokchon or a traditional Korean set meal restaurant for a special occasion dinner (approx. ₩25,000–₩40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve (Sung-tan-jeol) is a major holiday in Korea — expect large crowds in Myeongdong and city center. Many restaurants offer special Christmas menus. Book dinner in advance if possible. The city is beautifully decorated and very atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nami Island (남이섬) — a stunning tree-lined island about 1.5 hours from Seoul, famous for its beautiful winter scenery and K-drama filming locations (Winter Sonata). Take the ferry across to the island and enjoy a peaceful morning walk through the snow-dusted tree corridors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nami Island — rent a bicycle, visit the art installations, and enjoy the peaceful natural beauty. Optionally combine with a visit to nearby Petite France (쁘띠프랑스) — a charming French-themed cultural village — or the Garden of Morning Calm (아침고요수목원), famous for its winter illumination festival.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul in the evening. Enjoy a relaxed Christmas night dinner and explore the city's Christmas illuminations along Cheonggyecheon or at major department stores (Lotte, Shinsegae).

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Nami Island
meals.lunch: Nami Island has several restaurants and cafés on-site — try a warm Korean meal or Western options available on the island (approx. ₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Back in Seoul — celebrate Christmas with a Korean BBQ feast at a mid-range restaurant. Try Maple Tree House or a local samgyeopsal (pork belly BBQ) spot (approx. ₩20,000–₩30,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island entry: ₩16,000 (includes ferry). Take ITX-Cheongchun train from Yongsan Station to Gapyeong Station, then taxi to Nami Island ferry dock. Book train tickets in advance on Korail website. Garden of Morning Calm has a spectacular winter light festival (Lights of the Starry Night) — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Seongsu-dong (성수동) neighborhood — Seoul's coolest up-and-coming district, often called the 'Brooklyn of Seoul.' Wander through converted factory spaces turned into art galleries, specialty coffee roasters, and concept stores. Visit the Daelim Warehouse or local art exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — Asia's largest indoor theme park — for a fun afternoon of rides and entertainment. Alternatively, visit the Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123rd floor) for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul in winter. Also explore the adjacent Seokchon Lake with its winter decorations.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening exploration — visit Dongdaemun Market for some last-minute shopping and the vibrant night market atmosphere. Browse the massive fashion wholesale markets, then enjoy a final street food crawl through the area.

meals.breakfast: Seongsu-dong specialty coffee shop — try a third-wave coffee roaster like Fritz Coffee Company or Namusairo for excellent coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Seongsu-dong — try a trendy brunch restaurant or Korean fusion spot in a converted factory space (approx. ₩15,000–₩22,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — try a hearty Korean meal of galbitang or seolleongtang at a local restaurant, or explore the pojangmacha street food tents for a fun final evening (approx. ₩12,000–₩18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory tickets: approx. ₩27,000. The observatory is open until 11 PM and offers stunning night views. Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot — it's a compact, walkable neighborhood with new spots opening regularly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — visit Namdaemun Market (남대문시장), one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets (open from early morning). Browse for last-minute souvenirs, Korean snacks to bring home (dried seaweed, instant ramen, Korean sweets), and traditional crafts. Great atmosphere and excellent prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit one final spot: the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) — a free, world-class museum in Yongsan covering Korean military history, or take a final walk through a favorite neighborhood. Begin packing and preparing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Incheon International Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in, immigration, and security. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport's many restaurants — try a bowl of bibimbap or Korean ramen at one of the airport's sit-down restaurants before departure.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — try hotteok (sweet syrup-filled pancakes), kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup), or a steaming bowl of haejang-guk (hangover soup) from a market vendor (approx. ₩5,000–₩10,000)
meals.lunch: Final Korean lunch — treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal. Try Gwangjang Market for one last bibimbap or a Korean set meal at a restaurant near your hotel (approx. ₩12,000–₩20,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — excellent food options including Korean BBQ, bibimbap, and international cuisine. Budget approx. ₩15,000–₩25,000 for airport dining

day_by_day.notes: Return your T-money card at the airport for a refund (minus ₩500 handling fee). Keep receipts for VAT refund — foreign visitors can claim tax refunds at the airport for purchases over ₩30,000 at participating stores. AREX Express Train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes 43 minutes (₩9,500). Allow extra time during holiday period.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Meet your private chauffeur at the arrivals hall for a luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome amenity and late-night room service.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at the resort — request Korean late-night staples such as juk (rice porridge) or ramyeon from the 24-hour kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — no activities scheduled before 22:30. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in preparation so the room is fully ready upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely start with a premium breakfast at the resort. Take a private guided morning walk through Gyeongbokgung Palace, the largest of the Five Grand Palaces, including a viewing of the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard at 10:00. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a premium rental shop near the palace for an immersive royal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses with sweeping views of the city. Arrange a private cultural workshop — options include hanji (traditional paper craft) or a tea ceremony at one of the village's heritage houses.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for curated shopping at high-end Korean craft galleries and artisan boutiques. Dine at a renowned traditional Korean restaurant for a royal court cuisine (Joseon-era hanjeongsik) multi-course dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Korean and Western buffet or à la carte options
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — award-winning temple food restaurant near Insadong offering refined Buddhist vegetarian cuisine
meals.dinner: Jihwaja — a prestigious restaurant specializing in royal court cuisine (hanjeongsik) with seasonal, premium ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung opens at 09:00. Changing of the Guard occurs at 10:00 and 14:00. Book hanbok rental in advance for the best selection. Reserve Jihwaja well ahead — it books quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden is particularly magical in winter with frost-covered pavilions and frozen ponds. Limit of visitors makes this an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jongno and Ikseon-dong districts — a trendy alley neighborhood blending Joseon-era architecture with contemporary Korean café culture, boutique shops, and art spaces. Visit a premium Korean skincare flagship store for a personalized consultation and shopping experience.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) at dusk via private cable car. Enjoy panoramic night views of the glittering Seoul cityscape. Dinner at N Grill, the revolving fine-dining restaurant at the top of the tower.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Ikseon Gonggan — a curated Korean fusion lunch at one of Ikseon-dong's premium heritage hanok restaurants
meals.dinner: N Grill at N Seoul Tower — French-inspired fine dining with 360° rotating views of Seoul's skyline

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are limited and must be booked in advance online. N Grill reservations are essential — request a window table for best views.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day K-culture immersion experience: visit a top-tier K-pop entertainment company district (HYBE, SM, or YG area in Gangnam/Mapo). Arrange a behind-the-scenes cultural tour, visit the HYBE Insight Museum — an interactive K-pop cultural museum with exclusive exhibitions on BTS and other artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the upscale Gangnam district for luxury shopping along Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Garosu-gil — Seoul's most fashionable boulevard lined with designer boutiques, Korean luxury fashion brands, and concept stores. Visit a premium Korean beauty flagship for a bespoke skincare treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live K-pop or traditional Korean performance. Options include a NANTA show (high-energy Korean percussion performance) or a traditional gugak concert at the National Gugak Center. Dinner at a Michelin-starred Gangnam restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Dosan Park area café-restaurant — modern Korean cuisine in a stylish Apgujeong setting
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul — Michelin two-star contemporary Korean fine dining with a creative tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight Museum tickets sell out quickly — book online well in advance. Check performance schedules at the National Gugak Center ahead of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) premium private tour. Depart early with a private guide and luxury vehicle. Visit the Third Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory (closest civilian point to North Korea), and Dorasan Station — the southernmost train station on the Korean Peninsula. A deeply moving and historically significant experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue DMZ exploration — visit the Imjingak Peace Park and the Bridge of Freedom. Reflect on Korea's divided history with expert commentary from your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by early evening. Relax at the resort's spa or wellness facilities. Quiet, reflective dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early packed premium breakfast from the resort or en-route stop
meals.lunch: Premium bento-style lunch box prepared by the resort or a curated stop at a local restaurant near Paju
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — indulge in a seasonal Korean tasting menu to wind down after a full day

day_by_day.notes: The DMZ tour requires advance passport registration. Depart by 07:30 to maximize time. Photography restrictions apply in certain areas — your guide will advise. This is a full and emotionally engaging day — keep the evening relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Private hands-on Korean cooking class with a master chef — learn to prepare iconic dishes such as kimchi, japchae, galbi (grilled short ribs), and doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew). Classes held in a premium culinary studio in central Seoul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's oldest and most vibrant traditional markets. Explore the street food stalls with your private guide, sampling bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare). A sensory deep-dive into local food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy Seongsu-dong district — Seoul's 'Brooklyn,' known for its converted industrial spaces, artisan coffee roasters, and concept boutiques. Dinner at a celebrated Korean BBQ restaurant for a premium grilling experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market food tour — curated tastings of traditional Korean street food with a private guide
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House — premium Korean BBQ using Wagyu and top-grade Korean hanwoo beef, Itaewon

day_by_day.notes: Cooking class ingredients and recipes are provided — dietary restrictions can be accommodated with advance notice. Gwangjang Market is busiest midday — arrive with an appetite.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Experience the peaceful morning atmosphere, observe monks in prayer, and learn about Korean Buddhist traditions. If December 21 aligns with a Buddhist ceremony, this is a rare and beautiful cultural opportunity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tour the National Museum of Korea — one of Asia's largest museums with an extraordinary collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. Arrange a private docent-led tour for an in-depth cultural experience. Visit the museum's premium gift shop for curated Korean art and design items.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to Naksan Park for panoramic views of the old city walls and Seoul's skyline. Dinner in the hip Hyehwa (Daehangno) district, known for its theatrical arts culture and intimate dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Museum restaurant or nearby Yongsan premium Korean restaurant
meals.dinner: Mingles — Michelin-starred restaurant blending Korean tradition with modern global techniques (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays. Verify the date falls on an open day. Mingles is one of Seoul's most sought-after reservations — book weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon — a UNESCO World Heritage Site 30 minutes from Seoul by KTX train. Private guided tour of Hwaseong Fortress, an 18th-century walled fortress with stunning architecture. Walk the full 5.7km fortress wall circuit for breathtaking winter views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (Hwaseong Haenggung) — the temporary palace used by King Jeongjo during royal visits. Watch a traditional archery demonstration and martial arts performance within the palace grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Spend the evening in the vibrant Hongdae district — the epicenter of Korean indie music, street art, and youth culture. Explore live music venues and contemporary art galleries before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi — Suwon is nationally famous for its galbi (grilled beef ribs). Dine at a top local galbi house near the fortress
meals.dinner: Hongdae area — Yeonnam-dong's premium Korean fusion restaurant or a curated omakase Korean dining experience

day_by_day.notes: KTX or express bus to Suwon takes approximately 30 minutes. A private car transfer is available for added comfort. Hwaseong Fortress is stunning in winter — wear warm layers for the wall walk.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury spa morning at the resort or a premium jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse) experience at Dragon Hill Spa — a world-class multi-floor Korean spa facility. Enjoy jade saunas, salt rooms, and traditional Korean body scrub (Italy towel exfoliation) treatments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lotte World Tower and Lotte World Mall — one of the world's tallest skyscrapers. Head to the SKY118 observation deck for spectacular views of Seoul. Explore the luxury retail floors and visit the Lotte Museum of Art for a premium contemporary art experience.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve celebrations in Seoul — enjoy the festive winter illuminations along Cheonggyecheon Stream, a beautifully lit urban waterway in the heart of the city. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant with views of the illuminated city.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lotte World Mall premium food hall — curated Korean and international fine dining options
meals.dinner: Ciel Bleu or a top-floor Lotte Hotel restaurant — French-Korean fusion fine dining with city views

day_by_day.notes: Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours — morning visits are less crowded. Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautifully decorated for the winter holiday season with light installations.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Deoksugung Palace — uniquely open for a nighttime illumination event in winter. Morning visit to experience the palace's Western-style Seokjojeon building and the Deoksugung Stone Wall Road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil), one of Seoul's most romantic walking paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Myeongdong district for premium Korean cosmetics shopping at flagship stores (Sulwhasoo, Innisfree, Amorepacific). Visit the Myeongdong Cathedral — one of Korea's most iconic Catholic churches, beautifully decorated for Christmas Eve.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — experience the magical festive atmosphere. Attend a Christmas Eve concert or special performance at the Seoul Arts Center or Lotte Concert Hall. Celebratory Christmas Eve dinner at one of Seoul's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — iconic Korean restaurant famous for its handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings)
meals.dinner: La Yeon — Michelin three-star Korean fine dining at The Shilla Hotel, Seoul's most prestigious dining experience

day_by_day.notes: La Yeon is Seoul's only Michelin three-star restaurant — reservations must be made months in advance. Christmas Eve in Seoul is festive and lively — the city is beautifully decorated. Confirm concert tickets well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — begin with a special Christmas breakfast at the resort. Private morning visit to Namsan Botanical Garden or a peaceful winter walk through Seoul Forest (Ttukseom), a beautiful urban park along the Han River, serene and uncrowded on Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Asia's premier private art museums featuring an extraordinary collection of Korean traditional art and contemporary international works. Arranged private curator-led tour for an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner celebration — a special multi-course Christmas dinner at the resort's premier restaurant or at one of Seoul's top international fine-dining establishments. Toast the holiday with premium Korean makgeolli or champagne.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at the resort — request a festive menu in advance
meals.lunch: Leeum Museum café or nearby Hannam-dong premium restaurant — Hannam-dong is Seoul's most upscale dining neighborhood
meals.dinner: Special Christmas dinner at Gaon — Michelin three-star Korean fine dining celebrating seasonal Korean ingredients with royal court traditions

day_by_day.notes: Some attractions may have limited hours on Christmas Day — verify in advance. Seoul celebrates Christmas as a public holiday. Gaon requires advance reservation and is one of Korea's most prestigious dining destinations.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the War Memorial of Korea — a powerful and comprehensive museum documenting Korea's military history, including the Korean War. An essential cultural and historical experience with world-class exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Itaewon and Hanam-dong neighborhoods — Seoul's most internationally cosmopolitan areas. Visit concept stores, antique dealers, and international galleries. Stop at a premium Korean ceramics studio for a private pottery experience or purchase artisan pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration in Gangnam — visit the COEX Starfield Library (one of the world's most stunning libraries inside a mall) and the COEX Aquarium. Dinner at a celebrated Gangnam fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Itaewon premium international restaurant — Seoul's most diverse dining neighborhood with exceptional global cuisine options
meals.dinner: Jungsik — Michelin two-star contemporary Korean restaurant in Gangnam, pioneering modern Korean cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The COEX Starfield Library is a spectacular architectural and cultural space — ideal for photography. Book Jungsik well in advance. Consider purchasing artisan ceramics or lacquerware as premium souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — leisurely breakfast at the resort. Last-minute luxury shopping at Shinsegae Department Store (the world's largest department store) or Hyundai The Hyundai Seoul for premium Korean goods, fashion, and gourmet food items to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — final stroll along the Han River or a visit to a rooftop café in Yongsan for one last panoramic view of Seoul. Return to the resort for luggage collection and private chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Access the premium airport lounge for a comfortable pre-flight experience. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Korean culture, cuisine, and luxury.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor a full Korean spread one last time
meals.lunch: Shinsegae Department Store premium food hall or a final Korean restaurant lunch near the hotel
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Incheon Airport check-in and security. The Incheon Airport premium lounges (including Korean Air's Prestige Lounge and Asiana's Business Lounge) offer excellent food and relaxation facilities. Confirm private transfer timing with the hotel concierge the evening before.
